evals.prompt: I need to log in to APIMatic CLI so I can build my developer portal. Can you walk me through the authentication process?
evals.expected_output: The agent runs the `auth-login.mjs` launcher (which starts `apimatic auth login`), explicitly tells the user a browser window has opened and waits for the user to confirm sign-in is complete before proceeding, then verifies with `apimatic auth status`.

assertions.description: Response starts the browser sign-in (the auth-login.mjs launcher, which runs `apimatic auth login`)
Response explicitly tells the user a browser window has opened
Response pauses and asks the user to confirm sign-in is complete before proceeding
Response includes `apimatic auth status` as a verification step after login

evals.prompt: I have my OpenAPI spec at ~/projects/petstore.yaml and I've never set up an APIMatic portal before. Help me create one from scratch.
evals.expected_output: The agent downloads the v2 branch of the sample portal repo, extracts src/ into the project directory, replaces the sample spec with the user's petstore.yaml, and starts the preview server. It does NOT download the master (v1) branch and does NOT run `apimatic quickstart`.

assertions.description: Response downloads the v2 branch of the sample portal
Response does NOT download the v1 master branch
Response extracts or copies the src/ directory
Response replaces the sample spec with petstore.yaml
Response does NOT run the interactive quickstart wizard

evals.prompt: My APIMatic portal project lives at ~/my-portal/ and it has a src/ folder inside it. I want to start the local dev server with hot reload. What commands should I run?
evals.expected_output: The agent works from ~/my-portal/ (the directory containing src/, not inside src/) and starts the preview with the serve.mjs script, which runs `apimatic portal serve`.

assertions.description: Response starts the preview server
Response instructs navigation to ~/my-portal/ (project root), not inside src/
Response does NOT tell the user to navigate into src/ before running portal serve

evals.prompt: I'm configuring a GitHub Actions CI pipeline to build and deploy my APIMatic portal. I have an API key from the APIMatic dashboard. How do I run the portal build step without requiring browser-based login?
evals.expected_output: The agent recommends `apimatic portal generate --auth-key=...` with the key from a repository secret, sets up Node 24 in the workflow, and uses @apimatic/cli@beta. It does not suggest browser-based login.

assertions.description: Response uses apimatic portal generate
Response passes the API key with --auth-key
Response uses the v2 CLI via @apimatic/cli@beta
Response sets up Node 24 in CI
Response does NOT use browser login in CI

evals.prompt: I want to add an API recipe to my APIMatic portal. How do I scaffold one using the CLI?
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that API Recipes are not available in APIMatic CLI v2 and offers a supported alternative such as a Markdown guide page. It does not invent recipe configuration.

assertions.description: Response says recipes are not available in this CLI version
Response does NOT tell the user to run the removed recipe wizard
Response does NOT invent recipe configuration
Response offers a guide page as an alternative

evals.prompt: Change my portal's brand color to #FF5733 and use our logo, which is at ./assets/logo.png.
evals.expected_output: The agent copies the logo into src/static/ and sets portal.brand.logo to a static/... path and portal.brand.colors.primary to #FF5733 in src/apimatic.json.

assertions.description: Response edits src/apimatic.json
Response sets colors.primary
Response uses the requested hex value
Response references the logo as a static/ path
Response does NOT use v1 theme keys

evals.prompt: I want my portal to be dark mode only, without the light/dark toggle.
evals.expected_output: The agent sets portal.brand.colorMode to "dark" in src/apimatic.json, which hides the theme switch.

assertions.description: Response uses brand.colorMode
Response sets it to dark
Response does NOT use v1 settings

evals.prompt: I'm completely new to APIMatic and want to build my first developer portal from scratch.
evals.expected_output: The agent follows Path A: runs `node --version` directly and checks for v24 or later, asks permission before installing @apimatic/cli@beta, then signs in and waits for browser sign-in confirmation before proceeding.

assertions.description: Response includes running `node --version` as the first check
Response checks for Node 24 or later
Response asks user permission before running npm install
Response installs the v2 CLI with @beta
Response starts the browser sign-in (the auth-login.mjs launcher, which runs `apimatic auth login`)
Response waits for user to confirm browser sign-in before proceeding

evals.prompt: I ran npm install -g @apimatic/cli but when I run apimatic --version it still says command not found.
evals.expected_output: The agent tells the user to install the v2 CLI with @beta (running it in their own terminal, without the agent retrying under sudo) and does NOT proceed to authentication or portal generation until the CLI is verified.

assertions.description: Response uses npm install -g @apimatic/cli@beta
Response does NOT run or suggest the install with sudo
Response does NOT proceed to authentication
Response does NOT run quickstart

evals.prompt: I completed browser sign-in for APIMatic but when I run apimatic auth status it doesn't show my email.
evals.expected_output: The agent offers the API key fallback (`apimatic auth login --auth-key=YOUR_API_KEY`) and does NOT proceed to portal generation until authentication is confirmed.

assertions.description: Response offers the --auth-key fallback
Response tells user where to find their API key
Response does NOT proceed to quickstart or portal generation while auth is unconfirmed

evals.prompt: The portal server is running. How do I stop it?
evals.expected_output: The agent runs `serve.mjs stop` directly to stop the server — it does NOT ask the user to run the stop command themselves.

assertions.description: Response includes serve.mjs stop command
Response does NOT tell the user to run the stop command themselves as the primary action
Response confirms the server was stopped or the port will be freed

evals.prompt: Add a custom markdown page called overview.md to my APIMatic portal guides.
evals.expected_output: The agent creates src/content/guides/overview.md starting with front matter that sets a title, adds "overview" (no extension) to guides/nav.json if that file lists pages explicitly, and restarts the preview because a page was added. It does NOT use toc.yml.

assertions.description: Response creates the page under content/guides/
Response gives the page a title in front matter
Response mentions nav.json for ordering
Response restarts the preview after adding a page
Response does NOT use toc.yml
Response does NOT put the file extension in nav.json

evals.prompt: In my portal's guides folder, I want the Authentication page to come before Quickstart in the sidebar.
evals.expected_output: The agent edits src/content/guides/nav.json so "authentication" is listed before "quickstart", using bare page names without extensions.

assertions.description: Response edits nav.json
Response lists authentication in pages
Response does NOT use file extensions in nav.json
Response does NOT use toc.yml

evals.prompt: Add a 'Status' link to my portal header that goes to https://status.acme.com.
evals.expected_output: The agent adds { "label": "Status", "url": "https://status.acme.com" } to portal.navigation.links in src/apimatic.json.

assertions.description: Response uses portal.navigation.links
Response sets the label
Response uses the requested URL
Response does NOT create a custom header HTML file

evals.prompt: Add cards to my portal overview page. Include a Card that links to my getting started guide at src/content/guides/getting-started.md.
evals.expected_output: The agent adds a <Cards> block with a <Card> whose href is the page URL /guides/getting-started. It does NOT use v1 syntax like <CardGroup> or page: links.

assertions.description: Response uses the Cards/Card components
Response uses href on the card
Response links to the page URL
Response does NOT use v1 card syntax

evals.prompt: I have an older APIMatic portal project with src/APIMATIC-BUILD.json and src/content/toc.yml. Help me upgrade it to the new CLI.
evals.expected_output: The agent follows the upgrade guide: installs @apimatic/cli@beta on Node 24, creates src/apimatic.json from the portal settings, adds title front matter to every page, replaces toc.yml with nav.json files, and tells the user which v1 features have no v2 equivalent.

assertions.description: Response creates src/apimatic.json
Response replaces toc.yml with nav.json
Response adds title front matter to pages
Response installs the v2 CLI
Response mentions Node 24

evals.prompt: My portal only shows the TypeScript SDK. Add Python and C# SDKs too.
evals.expected_output: The agent adds "python": {} and "csharp": {} to the languages block of src/apimatic.json and restarts the preview, since adding a language needs a restart.

assertions.description: Response edits the languages block
Response adds python
Response adds csharp
Response restarts the preview
Response does NOT use v1 template names

evals.prompt: Add a Java SDK to my APIMatic portal.
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that only C#, Python, and TypeScript are available in the portal today and does not add java to the languages block.

assertions.description: Response says Java is not available
value: is not something i can add

assertions.description: Response names the supported languages
Response does NOT add java to languages

evals.prompt: I want to enable API Copilot for my portal.
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that API Copilot is not part of APIMatic CLI v2's portal configuration and does not invent configuration for it.

assertions.description: Response says Copilot is not available
Response does NOT invent copilot configuration

evals.prompt: Set up SEO and LLMs.txt for my portal. It will be hosted at https://developers.acme.com.
evals.expected_output: The agent sets portal.site.url to https://developers.acme.com and explains that sitemap.xml, robots.txt, llms.txt and llms-full.txt are generated automatically.

assertions.description: Response sets the site URL
Response uses portal.site
Response says llms.txt is generated automatically
Response does NOT use v1 SEO keys

evals.prompt: Remove the buttons on each page that open it in ChatGPT or other AI assistants.
evals.expected_output: The agent sets portal.ai.pageActions to false in src/apimatic.json.

assertions.description: Response uses pageActions
Response sets it to false

evals.prompt: Put the API Reference tab before the SDKs tab in my portal.
evals.expected_output: The agent edits src/content/nav.json and places "apimatic:api" before "apimatic:sdks" in the root file's tabs list (not in pages).

assertions.description: Response edits nav.json
Response uses the apimatic:api token
Response uses the apimatic:sdks token
Response orders the tabs with the tabs key

evals.prompt: Add a Context Plugin page to my portal so developers can use my API from Claude Code and Cursor.
evals.expected_output: The agent explains the SDKs must be published with source code first, records pluginId/pluginName/pluginVersion in the plugin block of src/apimatic.json, runs apimatic plugin generate, and restarts the preview so the Context Plugin tab appears.

assertions.description: Response requires publishing SDKs with source code
Response runs apimatic plugin generate
Response records the plugin identity
Response does NOT use v1 aiIntegration settings

evals.prompt: How do I deploy my APIMatic portal to Netlify?
evals.expected_output: The agent runs apimatic portal generate with --destination, explains the output folder is a static site to upload to Netlify, points unknown paths at 404.html, and sets portal.site.url to the production address.

assertions.description: Response runs apimatic portal generate
Response uses --destination
Response mentions 404.html
Response sets the production site URL

evals.prompt: I added a new page at src/content/faq.md but it doesn't show up in the portal preview.
evals.expected_output: The agent checks the page starts with front matter that sets a title and restarts the preview, because adding a page needs a restart.

assertions.description: Response checks for title front matter
Response restarts the preview

evals.prompt: apimatic portal serve refuses to run and says my Node.js version is 22.
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that APIMatic CLI v2 needs Node.js 24 or later and points the user to nodejs.org.

assertions.description: Response says Node 24 or later is needed
Response points to the Node.js download page

evals.prompt: Our portal won't get its own subdomain. It will live at https://acme.com/developers on our main site. What do I need to change?
evals.expected_output: The agent sets portal.site.url to the full address https://acme.com/developers, restarts the preview because the path changed, rebuilds with apimatic portal generate, and explains that the build must be served at /developers with 404.html for missing pages under it, and that no robots.txt is generated so the sitemap line goes in the root robots.txt.

assertions.description: Response sets site.url to the address with the path
Response restarts the preview after changing the path
Response says to serve 404.html under the path
Response explains the robots.txt / sitemap handling
Response does NOT use v1 baseUrl

evals.prompt: After updating the APIMatic CLI, my portal's tab bar disappeared. The Guides folder, API Reference and SDKs now show up in the sidebar, and portal serve warns that src/content/nav.json has no tabs. My nav.json is {"pages": ["index", "guides", "apimatic:api", "apimatic:sdks"]}.
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that only what the root nav.json lists in tabs is a tab, moves guides, apimatic:api, and apimatic:sdks from pages to a tabs list (a name cannot be in both), and confirms the preview picks up the change.

assertions.description: Response adds a tabs key
Response keeps Guides as a tab
Response keeps the API reference as a tab
Response does NOT use toc.yml

evals.prompt: OAuth sign-in in my portal's API playground fails: the provider says the redirect URI doesn't match. The portal is at https://docs.acme.com.
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that the playground's OAuth sign-in returns to one page, /oauth/callback, and tells the user to register https://docs.acme.com/oauth/callback as a redirect URI with their OAuth provider.

assertions.description: Response gives the callback address
Response tells the user to register it with the provider

evals.expected_output: The agent tells the user that CLI v1 (1.5.0) is installed and that it is upgrading the APIMatic CLI to v2 with npm install -g @apimatic/cli@beta, mentions how to switch back to v1, verifies apimatic --version, then starts the preview.

Response upgrades with npm install -g @apimatic/cli@beta
